focus: only the fixes since build 24: ConnectChambers carve-as-you-go, the pinch ring check, BlocksOf stuff check, saveCompressible removal, filthLeaving IsNull
diffSource: since build 24 (2026-10-09T23:47:58Z), the last reviewed build, from the build log

findings.title: Old saves with an open dungeon lose every wall once TUBAD_DungeonWall stops being saveCompressible
findings.detail: On load, MapFileCompressor.ThingsToSpawnAfterLoad still finds the wall's short hash in any save made on build 24 or earlier. Because thingDef.saveCompressible is now false, it logs 'Tried loading non-compressible thing as compressed thing' once per wall cell and does not spawn the wall, so a dungeon that was open in the save comes back with no walls. The fix itself is right: before it, each wall reloaded through MakeThing(def) with no stuff, logging an error and taking a default stone. If any build 24 or earlier ever reached players, one remedy is to re-place missing walls when a dungeon map loads (the site keeps its layout and every closed cell is a wall). Otherwise, say in the changelog that dungeons open across this update should be left first. If nothing has shipped, ignore this.

findings.title: Adding the layer ID to the theme seed changes the theme of every tile in existing saves
findings.detail: Gen.HashCombineInt(seed, 0) is not the same as the old seed, so surface tiles also get a new roll. A save from before this build will see different themes on tiles it already visited, a one-time break of the 'same tile, same theme' promise. That's fine before release; after release it belongs in the changelog.

findings.title: The ice plug still inherits Filth_RubbleRock
findings.detail: Only TUBAD_RootTangle and TUBAD_SandDrift clear filthLeaving. TUBAD_IcePlug keeps BuildingNaturalBase's Filth_RubbleRock, so mining or damaging ice leaves rock rubble. That may be on purpose; it's an opinion, not a defect.

findings.title: A chamber nothing can reach now gets retried against every other group during the spanning tree
findings.detail: Before, the spanning tree carved only its chosen links. Now every pair that joins two groups is tried until one carves. If a chamber can't be reached at all, each attempt either fails fast in TryDoor or runs a full-map A* before failing, once per pair. That's acceptable at current chamber counts, but it is where to look if map generation ever stalls.

Pinch ring path check: indices p-3..p+3 stay in bounds because p runs from 3 to Count-4; the loop over the whole path skips only the squeeze cells p-2..p+2
